description: HUD's Low-Income Housing Tax Credit database lists 55,345 affordable rental housing projects with 3.9 million housing units placed in service in the United States between 1987 and 2024. For each project it gives the address, the number of units and of low-income units, bedrooms, the year the credit was allocated and the year the project was placed in service, whether it was new construction or rehabilitation, the type of credit and other financing sources, and the records are geocoded. The LIHTC programme gives state and local agencies about 12 billion US dollars a year in tax credits for rental housing for lower-income households. The whole database is one ZIP with a CSV, an Access database that also holds building addresses from the tenant data collection, and a data dictionary; a query system selects projects by state, city, county or radius. The program page was revised on 28 May 2026, and 2025 projects will be added in spring 2027. Format and access: free download, no registration shown. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: almost every variable is missing for some projects, and from the cloud the ZIP returned HTTP 202 with no content (a bot check), so the file itself was not opened. Simulation uses: locating subsidised multifamily housing for exposure and equity analysis of hazards and outages, and for housing capacity in agent-based models. Related records: the American Housing Survey and the HUD CDBG-DR disaster recovery grants.
